rationale: C08 has the closest structural resemblance: a presidential letter grounded in departmental studies that treats an existing tax benefit or burden as obsolete, anticipates congressional action, and links tax-law revision to a broader policy change. But its language and operative sequence are not distinctive enough to show material reuse. C17 concerns the precise silver statutes, Treasury authority, and silver-bullion tax implicated by the child, but it is a delegation order supplying legal background rather than a drafting template. C05 is another Kennedy monetary-policy letter combining Treasury action with proposed legislation, yet its shared features are generic. No candidate plausibly supplied a concrete, material portion of the child's drafting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: On the basis of your recommendations and the studies conducted by the Treasury and other Departments... I intend to recommend to Congress... [repeal of silver acts and the relevant portion of the Internal Revenue Code].
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The tax treatment accorded this industry... has been the subject of recent studies by both the Treasury Department and the Department of Commerce... [and] will be considered promptly upon the convening of the next session of the Congress.
shared_material.explanation: C08 shares a studies-to-tax-revision-to-congressional-action structure, but the wording and machinery remain too general to establish template reuse.

shared_material.child_excerpt: repeal the acts relating to silver of June 19, 1934... [and] the existing tax on transfers of interest in silver bullion
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the act of June 19, 1934... [and] section 1805 of the Internal Revenue Code... (with respect to silver bullion)
shared_material.explanation: C17 identifies the same silver-specific legal framework, but does not contribute the child's policy-announcement form, language, or operative sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: you are directed to suspend further sales of free silver... I intend to recommend to Congress...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The draft bill implements a recommendation... It also complements and supports my directive to the Secretary of the Treasury...
shared_material.explanation: C05 similarly combines a Treasury directive with a legislative proposal in monetary policy, but this is a broad administrative pattern rather than distinctive shared drafting.
